text:
sam: Heads-up: linkcheck flagged a weird class of broken anchors that only show up on pages that use the include/snippet pattern. Example: /examples/streams#client-connection jumps to top because actual generated id is client-connection-1.

maria: Repro'd. The include template is rendering the same heading twice (one from the parent page, one from the included snippet), so Docusaurus/mkdocs adds a -1 suffix to make the id unique. Our old internal links target the base id (without -1).

sam: Right. So the symptom is: links that reference the canonical heading (no suffix) fail when the included snippet introduces a duplicate. You only see the -1 in the rendered HTML id.

frank: Is the root cause the snippet content having the same h2/h3 as the parent? We could change include behavior to strip heading levels or add a `no-heading` frontmatter to snippets.

maria: Two mitigation options: 1) Add explicit ids in the parent (e.g., `### Client connection {#client-connection}`), 2) Add a small preprocessor that detects duplicate ids and normalizes them by preferring the parent's id and rewriting the included file's heading id to a suffixed alias, plus emit a build warning.

lee: I worry about a preprocessor that rewrites content on the fly; it might confuse grep-based tooling and contributors. Prefer explicit ids where we have important anchors, and a linter that fails CI when a link points to an id that ends with -1 or -2.

sam: Fair. I wrote a quick script that scans the built HTML for ids that end in `-\d+` and traces back to the source file. It found 17 occurrences across guides/examples. Script:```bash
# find duplicate id suffixes in build dir
grep -rho "id=\\\"[^\"]*-\d+\\\"" build/ | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
```
It prints the duplicated ids and frequency.

frank: Nice. Can that script also map the id back to the source md file? If we can produce an actionable report for authors that would speed fixes.

maria: I extended it to use the search index and output `source: file.md -> id`. Will push as `scripts/find-duplicate-ids.sh` in my PR.

dev-docs-bot: Build preview started for PR 4412  linkcheck queued.

sam: PR 4412 (https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4412) includes: the `find-duplicate-ids.sh` script, fixes for the 7 highest-traffic pages (added explicit ids in the parent where anchors matter), and a short note in `docs/contrib/heading-ids.md` advising maintainers to add explicit ids for headings that are referenced elsewhere.

lee: I left a review comment suggesting we also add a CI job that runs `find-duplicate-ids.sh` and fails if it finds >0 duplicates with suffixes, so we don't regress.

frank: One corner-case: some snippets intentionally duplicate headings as part of example isolation. The script should allow an opt-out via `<!-- allow-duplicate-heading -->` comment in the snippet. Otherwise we will force authors to add ids everywhere.

maria: Good call. I added support for that opt-out comment; the linter will ignore items with that comment. Documented in the contrib page.

dev-docs-bot: Linkcheck completed: 2 warnings (external), 1 failure (internal anchor mismatch). See log: https://ci.redwood.ai/4412/linkcheck.log

sam: The failure points to `/examples/streams` -> `#client-connection` still referencing the base id while the page now contains `client-connection-1` because we missed adding explicit id to the parent for that page. I'll patch and push.

frank: Also left a suggestion to update the include template so it strips top-level headings when `strip_heading: true` is set in the include directive. That might avoid future duplicates.

lee: Agree that template change is valuable, but it's a bigger lift (affects many repos that consume snippets). Let's do parent explicit ids + find-duplicates CI first, then plan template change in Q2.

sam: Patch pushed. PR 4412 updated. dev-docs-bot: Linkcheck re-run.

dev-docs-bot: Linkcheck passed: 0 failures, 3 warnings (external). Preview published: https://deploy-preview-4412--docs.redwood.ai/examples/streams  build id 2026-04-02-10:17

maria: Merged PR 4412. Added a short migration note: "If you include snippets that contain headings, prefer explicit header ids in the parent page or use strip_heading on the snippet to avoid duplicate id suffixing."

frank: Thanks all. If you come across pages that still have `-1` style ids, paste them here and we'll triage.

sam: Closing thread, will file a follow-up issue to track the include-template work.
